messages:
alex chen: quick sync — did a pass on the prompt-sets approval flow mock. main thing: the bulk-approve CTA reads 'Approve selections' which feels wordy. also keyboard focus order seems off when you toggle compact diffs. tagging folks for microcopy + a11y
maria gonzalez: agree on the CTA. can we try 'Approve' for primary and 'Approve all' for a bulk action? shorter is clearer and fits smaller buttons. also saw low contrast on the disabled state for the approve-all checkbox @jamie park
jamie park: re: focus, the compact diff uses a grid of cards. when you tab, focus jumps into the card body before the selection checkbox. should be: checkbox -> card header -> diff preview. i'll attach an annotated flow in figma later :point_down:
olivia yu: accessibility nit: screen reader reads "card" for each diff with no context. we should add aria-label like "Prompt set diff for <test_name>, change summary" and aria-live for approval status updates so SR users hear when an item is approved. small change but big UX.
samir rao: noted. On the batching behavior: when you select multiple diffs and click Approve, we show the toast 'Approvals queued'. Product asked for a progress indicator. Suggest: replace with an inline progress bar + ability to cancel. thoughts?
alex chen: inline progress + cancel sounds good. for copy: toast should be "Approvals started" not 'queued' — queued implies it might not run. I'd also prefer CTA to say 'Approve (3)' when multiple selected.
maria gonzalez: microcopy iteration: primary: 'Approve (n)' secondary: 'Request changes' instead of 'Reject' maybe softer language. Also confirm wording for canary rollouts — if someone approves a prompt set it shouldn't auto-apply to production unless explicitly 'Rollout' is chosen.
jamie park: dev note — keyboard shortcut suggestion: 'A' for approve selection, 'R' for request changes, 'Space' toggles checkbox when focus is on a card. Need to ensure no conflicts with browser / screen reader shortcuts.
olivia yu: a11y: avoid single-letter shortcuts unless documented and opt-in. Users with assistive tech may intercept. Better: show shortcuts in a help popover and require holding modifier (Ctrl/Cmd) + A.
alex chen: good point. modifier + A it is. also we should add an aria-describedby on the bulk-approve CTA to list consequences: "Items approved will be marked approved and available for rollouts" — boring but explicit.
samir rao: backend question: when approving 200 items, do we batch into background job? We should surface a warning if selecting >50 and say 'This may take several minutes'.
jamie park: UI idea: disable 'Approve (n)' and replace with 'Start approvals (n)' when >50 and show expected ETA in tooltip. avoids false immediacy.
design-bot: Uploaded 1 image: compact-diff-focus-order.png
maria gonzalez: copy tweak for confirmation modal: header 'Approve selected prompt changes?' body: 'This will mark X test runs as approved. Approved items will be eligible for rollouts.' buttons: Primary 'Confirm approvals' Secondary 'Cancel'. prefer 'Confirm approvals' vs 'Approve' to reduce accidental clicks.
olivia yu: For screen reader clarity, add role="status" to the confirmation modal content so activation reads the summary.
alex chen: final asks: jamie, can you reorder focus in prototype and add modifier + shortcut hint in the header. maria, drop a short copy doc with the exact strings. olivia, can you create a failing axe test for the card labels? samir, can you confirm backend batch limits and error responses for partial failures.
maria gonzalez: will do, i'll paste copy here when ready. :thumbsup:
jamie park: i'll push a small prototype update by EOD and ping this thread. testing keyboard now.
samir rao: checking batch limits with infra — will report back by tomorrow. if partial failures, UI should show which items failed and let user retry.
alex chen: perfect. thanks team. follow-ups in thread only so we can keep the design PR linked.
